headline: Frozen protein and chemical embeddings scored against campaign-grouped, structure-aware benchmarks
label: Learned Enzyme And Variant Prioritization
summary: Enzyme kinetics, stability and binding-site predictors built on frozen PLM/CLM features are now judged by campaign-split benchmarks and experimental validation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is prioritizing enzymes, variants and ligand sites with representations lifted from pretrained protein and chemical models, increasingly fused with structure or dynamics. KineCouple applies substrate-conditioned cross-attention over frozen ProtT5/MolT5 features for kcat and Km; DecoyOpt uses ESM3-generated functional-site decoys for enzyme discrimination and EC assignment; StableProt couples SaProt with Foldseek 3Di tokens for Tm and OGT; DynamicsPLM adds residue-level and pairwise MD heads to a 35M-parameter model for zero-shot variant effects; EvoPhi-DDG plus JanusDDG enforces antisymmetric, thermodynamically consistent ddG. Structural conditioning extends to allosteric sites across apo/holo states, phosphosite function, RNA small-molecule pockets and partner-specific interfaces. What is new is the evaluation turn: EnzyArena groups kinetic data by engineering campaign, finds zero-shot consensus strongest and validates 150 mutants; cofolding benchmarks show ligand placement decoupled from protein conformation; NMR chemical shifts expose foundation-model errors at dynamic core residues.
